RFC6810-5.1-1.note: Forbidden: accepting a Prefix PDU whose Max Length is below its Prefix Length. TestParseIPv4PrefixMaxLenLessThanPrefixLen (prefix 24, max 16, otherwise valid) fails unless parseIPv4Prefix errors with "invalid"; the check sits in parsePrefixPDU, which the IPv6 parser shares. Positive: max 24 over prefix 8 yields a VRP with MaxLength 24.

RFC6810-5.1-3.note: The row covers every zero/reserved field of every PDU. TestRFC6810ReservedPrefixOctetsIgnored proves it for the IPv4 Prefix PDU only: an all-ones header zero field, reserved flag bits and zero octet still authorize the route, and clearing the announce bit withdraws it (so only reserved bits are ignored). No unit sends a nonzero reserved field in the other PDUs a router receives (Serial Notify, Cache Response, End of Data, Cache Reset, IPv6 Prefix), so a receiver that rejects those stays green. Same judgement as RFC8210-5-1.

RFC6810-6.1-1.note: {single-polarity: positive} carried on the row. TestRFC6810DefaultPollCadenceIsHourly asserts only that pollDelay(true) and pollDelay(false) return at most one hour on a fresh session. It does not drive Run, so a loop that ignored pollDelay and never re-queried would stay green, and nothing asserts that a v0 End of Data (which carries no timing parameters) leaves those intervals within the hour.

RFC6810-6.3-1.note: Forbidden: after a Cache Reset with no more-preferred cache, not issuing a Reset Query or not taking a whole new load. TestCacheResetTriggersResetQuery calls handlePDU directly and asserts only that s.serial becomes 0 and the sync ends; no tagged unit observes the Reset Query on the wire or the old set replaced by a full load. The negative (Serial Notify keeps the serial) holds. Same judgement as RFC8210-8.3-1.

RFC6810-6.4-1.note: Forbidden: stopping, or sending anything but a Reset Query, after No Data Available with no other cache. TestRFC6810NoDataAvailableRepeatsResetQuery runs one live cache that answers two queries with Error Report code 2 and asserts three consecutive received queries are pduResetQuery, each within 4s (t.Fatal on silence, assert.Equal on a Serial Query). Negative: once the cache supplies a load the route validates and the next query is pduSerialQuery, so the reset mode ends at the usable load.

RFC6810-7-1.note: {single-polarity: positive} carried on the row. TestParseRPKIConfigDefaults asserts only that a parsed cache-server with no port defaults to 323; no tagged unit drives an unprotected TCP RTR session from config to show ze implements the transport on that port. Same judgement as RFC8210-9-1.
